fathomable

/FATH-um-uh-bul/ — rhymes with 'atom-able' · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Something fathomable can be understood or figured out, even if it takes real effort.

Explained with pictures, the tax rules finally became fathomable.

Example

The quantum physics lecture initially seemed incomprehensible, but after working through detailed examples and running simulations, the underlying principles became fathomable.

Fathomable precisely captures the idea that something difficult and complex can still be understood through effort and study. A plain 'understandable' doesn't convey that sense of overcome difficulty—it just means 'able to be grasped.' Fathomable says 'yes, this is hard, but you can get there.'

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

understandable: Understandable is the plain word for anything the mind can grasp, and it says nothing about effort — a road sign is understandable at a glance. Fathomable carries a built-in struggle: something fathomable is hard, yet can be worked out with real study. Easy things are understandable; deep ones are fathomable.

comprehensible: Comprehensible means clear enough to make sense of now — the explanation already works and the reader is following it. Fathomable looks forward instead: the material still looks daunting, but effort will eventually crack it. A tidy textbook chapter is comprehensible; a dense proof you trust yourself to conquer is fathomable.

intelligible: Intelligible is mostly about form: speech or writing orderly enough to be made out — not garbled, not smeared. Fathomable is about depth: the words may be perfectly plain while the idea underneath takes long effort to reach. A mumble is unintelligible; a deep theory can still be fathomable.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

inscrutable: impossible to interpret or figure out

baffling: so confusing it cannot be figured out

Where it sits · how much effort understanding takes — obvious → clear → inscrutable → fathomable

obvious vs. fathomable: Obvious is far easier than fathomable: an obvious point needs no effort at all, while a fathomable one can be understood only after real work.

clear vs. fathomable: Clear is easier than fathomable — a clear explanation makes sense right away, while a fathomable one takes some digging before it finally makes sense.

inscrutable vs. fathomable: Inscrutable lies past the end of fathomable: a fathomable mystery can eventually be figured out, but an inscrutable one defeats every attempt to understand it.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — fathom

Root — fathom: outstretched arms; a six-foot measure of depth (Old English faethm) (Old English)

Suffix — -able

Suffix — -able: able to be, can be done (Latin (via Old French))

Put it together

Put it together: Fathom ('the span of outstretched arms,' used by sailors to measure the sea's depth) + -able ('can be done') builds 'able to be measured to the bottom' — a fathomable idea is one whose depths your mind can reach with effort.

Use the root in a new word: fathom

Use the root in a new word: fathom: Sailors once dropped a knotted rope to fathom the sea — to measure its depth by the span of two outstretched arms — so a fathomable idea is one whose depths your mind can reach.

Word Choice

neutral / educated

Reach for fathomable when describing something complex that has become understandable through study or effort—it emphasizes both the difficulty and the success. For something obviously simple, plain 'understandable' is clearer and better.
